To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of cross-document matching and the combination of the best performing features for sentence selection and ranking, respectively, lead to a better scientific text summarization system.

(i) the use of a sentence representation model based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) outperforms the use of a traditional vector space model (VSM) in the task of cross-document sentence matching; (ii) the use of an ensemble of CNN-based sentence representations improves the performance of the sentence representation model; and (iii) the use of CNN-based sentence representation models improves the performance of a scientific text summarization system.
the use of a cross-document sentence matching system can improve the performance of a scientific text summarization system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of two different but related tasks: cross-document sentence matching and scientific text summarization.
the development of a system for scientific text summarization, and a system for sentence matching in scientific documents.
developing and evaluating methods for cross-document sentence matching and scientific text summarization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LaSTUS/TALn team has achieved the best results for cross-document sentence matching and the second-best for scientific text summarization.
the LaSTUS/TALn systems were the most successful ones in the CL-SciSump 2017 task.
the results are promising and encouraging for the future development of these systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we participated in two different tasks, namely the Cross-document Sentence Matching task and the Scientific Text Summarisation task.
we have developed a new cross-document sentence matching system, LaSTUS, which is based on a novel approach to sentence representation, which we call sentence embedding.

the LaSTUS system is a cross-document sentence matching system that is able to extract the main information in a set of scientific documents, and the TALN system is a scientific text summarization system able to generate summaries of scientific documents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the two approaches (sentence matching and scientific text summarization) is a very promising direction.
the combination of different types of features (lexical, syntactic, semantic and statistical) can improve the performance of sentence matching systems.
the combination of a sentence similarity measure and a summarization model can lead to a competitive system in the CL-SciSump 2017 Task 2.
